<issue>
Heap Out-of-bounds Read in ISO9660 Virtual Directory Construction (isoent_tree)
#### Description
### Summary
A heap-based out-of-bounds read occurs in the ISO9660 writer during virtual parent directory construction. Specifically, in `isoent_tree()`, the function computes a substring length (`fn - p + l`) that may equal zero, causing an empty `archive_string` to be created. The subsequent code unconditionally evaluates `as.s[as.length - 1]`, which becomes a read from `as.s[-1]`, accessing one byte before the heap buffer. This leads to a deterministic crash when handling attacker-controlled pathnames, resulting in denial-of-service in applications that generate ISO9660 images from untrusted input.

We identified this bug in commit https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/commit/a819cc28299dca6cf455af074a1a7939efbfb13c. We privately reported this bug when the affected commit was still the latest version. As it has never been publicly disclosed or patched, we believe the vulnerability remains present in the current release.

### Details
The vulnerable code resides in isoent_tree() within archive_write_set_format_iso9660.c:
```c
			archive_string_init(&as);
			archive_strncat(&as, p, fn - p + l);
			if (as.s[as.length-1] == '/') { // here
				as.s[as.length-1] = '\0';
				as. length--;
			}
```
Here:

1. `fn` and `p` are pointers within the parent directory path string.
2. `l` is the length returned by `get_path_component()`.

Under certain malformed pathnames, the previous loop breaks when get_path_component() returns 0, leaving:
```
l == 0
fn == p
fn - p + l == 0
```
This causes:
`archive_strncat(&as, p, 0);`
to produce an empty string (as.length == 0). Immediately afterward, the code unconditionally checks:
`as.s[as.length - 1]`
which evaluates to:
`as.s[-1]`
reading 1 byte before the heap-allocated buffer.

### PoC
libarchive version: commit https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/commit/a819cc28299dca6cf455af074a1a7939efbfb13c
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
Compiler: clang version 14.0.0-1ubuntu1.1
configuration:
Build libarchive with ASan:
```
CC=clang
CXX=clang++
CFLAGS="-g -O1 -fsanitize=address"
CXXFLAGS="-g -O1 -fsanitize=address"
```
Compile the PoC:
```
clang -g -O1 -fsanitize=address \
    -I /path/to/libarchive \
    poc.c /path/to/libarchive.a \
    -lbz2 -llzma -lz -lxml2 -llz4 -lzstd \
    -o poc
```
Run the PoC:
```
./poc POC_FILE
```

#include <archive.h>
#include <archive_entry.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static la_ssize_t write_callback(struct archive *a, void *client_data, 
                                  const void *buffer, size_t length) {
    return length;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s <crash_file>\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    if (!f) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long len = ftell(f);
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
    
    unsigned char *buf = malloc(len);
    if (!buf) {
        fclose(f);
        return 1;
    }
    
    fread(buf, 1, len, f);
    fclose(f);
    
    struct archive *a = archive_write_new();
    if (!a) {
        free(buf);
        return 1;
    }
    
    int format = buf[0] % 5;
    switch (format) {
        case 0: archive_write_set_format_zip(a); break;
        case 1: archive_write_set_format_pax_restricted(a); break;
        case 2: archive_write_set_format_7zip(a); break;
        case 3: archive_write_set_format_gnutar(a); break;
        case 4: archive_write_set_format_iso9660(a); break;
    }
    
    int compression = buf[1] % 4;
    switch (compression) {
        case 0: archive_write_add_filter_gzip(a); break;
        case 1: archive_write_add_filter_bzip2(a); break;
        case 2: archive_write_add_filter_xz(a); break;
        case 3: break;
    }
    
    archive_write_open(a, NULL, NULL, write_callback, NULL);
    
    const uint8_t *ptr = buf + 2;
    size_t remaining = len - 2;
    
    while (remaining > 10) {
        struct archive_entry *entry = archive_entry_new();
        
        size_t name_len = ptr[0] % 100 + 1;
        if (name_len > remaining - 1) {
            name_len = remaining - 1;
        }
        
        char *pathname = malloc(name_len + 1);
        if (!pathname) {
            archive_entry_free(entry);
            break;
        }
        memcpy(pathname, ptr + 1, name_len);
        pathname[name_len] = '\0';
        
        archive_entry_set_pathname(entry, pathname);
        archive_entry_set_filetype(entry, AE_IFREG);
        archive_entry_set_perm(entry, 0644);
        
        ptr += name_len + 1;
        remaining -= name_len + 1;
        
        if (remaining < 2) {
            free(pathname);
            archive_entry_free(entry);
            break;
        }
        
        size_t content_len = (ptr[0] | (ptr[1] << 8)) % 1024;
        if (content_len > remaining - 2) {
            content_len = remaining - 2;
        }
        
        archive_entry_set_size(entry, content_len);
        
        if (archive_write_header(a, entry) == ARCHIVE_OK) {
            ptr += 2;
            remaining -= 2;
            
            if (content_len > 0 && content_len <= remaining) {
                archive_write_data(a, ptr, content_len);
                ptr += content_len;
                remaining -= content_len;
            }
        }
        
        free(pathname);
        archive_entry_free(entry);
        
        if (remaining < 10) break;
    }
    
    archive_write_close(a);
    archive_write_free(a);
    free(buf);
    
    printf("Test completed successfully\n");
    return 0;
}

content.text:
I fixed the out-of-bounds read in `isoent_tree()` in `libarchive/archive_write_set_format_iso9660.c`. The check now reads `if (as.length > 0 && as.s[as.length-1] == '/')`. When the computed substring length is zero, the code no longer reads `as.s[-1]`.

I haven't built it or run any tests, and I haven't tried the PoC file.

I didn't confirm that `as.s` is non-null for an empty string before it goes to `isoent_create_virtual_dir()`. I believe `archive_strncat` allocates the buffer even for a zero-length append, but I didn't verify that.
